extractor: read directly from the official IRCC pages listed in source_roles
policy: Every entry quotes the official page it was read from. source_excerpt is verbatim government wording, lowercased by the normalizer. Nothing here is paraphrased into a requirement, and nothing is included that the page did not state.
not_extracted: The registered 'landing' source (study-permit.html) states no requirements of its own — it is a section index. It repeats the fee as 'study permit: $can 150', which is taken from the fees page instead, so the role is left out of source_roles rather than cited for a claim it does not originate.

The inside-Canada and port-of-entry application branches. The apply page carries all three routes (outside Canada / inside Canada / at a port of entry) in one document and the normalizer flattens the selector, so the eligibility lists for the inside-Canada and port-of-entry routes cannot be cleanly attributed. Everything extracted here is either stated unconditionally or belongs to the outside-Canada route, which is what IMM 1294 is titled for.

Quebec's Certificat d'acceptation du Québec (CAQ). The documents page states students in Quebec need one instead of a PAL/TAL, but VisaAI has no fact for the province of study, so the condition is stated in the PAL/TAL description rather than encoded as a rule.
The PAL/TAL exceptions list. The documents page says exceptions exist and links out to them; the exceptions themselves are on a separate page that was not read.

Letter-of-acceptance exception for family members of an approved study or work permit applicant. The page states it, but VisaAI has no fact for 'accompanying an approved permit holder', so it is described on the requirement rather than gated.

Visa-office-specific additional documents. The documents page states 'there may be other documents to submit that are specific to your local visa office', but the list is per-country and behind a selector.
U.S. citizen and U.S. lawful permanent resident proof-of-identity alternatives. Branch-specific and linked out to another page.
Venezuelan passport-extension instructions. A nationality-specific branch on both the documents and apply pages; not attributable to the general route.
Processing times — the landing page says only 'varies by country' and publishes no number.

Which countries or territories require biometrics. IRCC gates that list behind a separate checker tool. The biometrics step here is gated on the age range the apply page states (14 to 79), which is the only part of the condition the page makes explicit.

Third-party costs for medical exams, police certificates, language testing and visa application centre services. The apply page names them but publishes no amounts — 'you won’t pay these fees in your online account. you’ll pay them directly to the third party.'

IRM 0002 (request for a change of sex or gender identifier). Named on the IMM 1294 page, but it applies only where the chosen gender identifier differs from an existing or foreign document, which VisaAI has no fact for.

IRCC's document checklist (IMM 5483). It is a PDF the sync cannot store as text (see 20261019220000), and canada.ca refused a direct download from the extraction host on 2026-10-20. The study permit rows below are quoted from the readable guide (IMM 5269), the IMM 1294 and IMM 5645 form pages, the documents page and the medical-exam country table instead.

Family Information (IMM 5707). Guide 5269's paper forms list names IMM 5707; IRCC's secure-account checklist for a study permit made outside Canada asks for IMM 5645 (recorded live on 2026-10-20). Both form pages carry the same 'who must complete' sentence; the form row is IMM 5645, the form the online application asks for.

The optional secure-account slots 'Schedule 1 - Application for a Temporary Resident Visa (IMM 5257 Schedule 1)' and 'Client Information'. Recorded live as optional on 2026-10-20, but no readable IRCC page states when either applies, so neither has a row.

The medical-exam trigger for work 'in a job in which public health must be protected'. VisaAI has no fact for an intended occupation in Canada, and a study permit is not a work application. The unconditional 'check if needed' step (medical_exam) still names all three triggers; the upload slot (proof_of_medical_exam) is gated on the stay-and-residence trigger guide 5269 states.

Travel to (rather than residence in) an IME country. IRCC's trigger is having 'lived in, or travelled to' a listed country for 6 months or more in a row in the year before coming. VisaAI's facts carry the current country of residence only, so the medical rows test that; an applicant who spent 6 months in a listed country but now lives elsewhere is not detected. For them the upload slot is excluded rather than 'may be required', and only the unconditional medical_exam step still points at the exam — recorded here as a known limit of the rule.

requirements.label: Letter of acceptance from your designated learning institution
requirements.description: IRCC marks this 'always required'. Your school gives it to you and you upload it to your online application. Post-secondary schools are asked to confirm the letter is valid; if the school does not respond by the deadline IRCC returns the application and refunds the processing fee. IRCC states one exception: family members of someone whose study or work permit application was approved in writing before they come to Canada do not need a letter of acceptance.
requirements.source_excerpt: get your letter of acceptance always required your school will give you a letter of acceptance. upload this to your online application.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Get your letter of acceptance Always required Your school will give you a letter of acceptance. Upload this to your online application.

requirements.label: Provincial attestation letter (PAL) or territorial attestation letter (TAL)
requirements.description: IRCC marks this 'needed in most cases'. In most cases you must accept your offer and pay your tuition fees, in part or in full, to get one. If you are studying in Quebec you need a Quebec acceptance certificate (certificat d’acceptation du Québec, CAQ) instead. IRCC states that exceptions to the PAL/TAL requirement exist; they are published on a separate page.
requirements.source_excerpt: apply for a provincial or territorial attestation letter needed in most cases get a provincial or territorial attestation letter (pal/tal) from your school. in most cases, you need to accept your offer and pay your tuition fees, either in part or in full, to get your pal/tal. if you’re studying in quebec , you need a quebec acceptance certificate ( certificat d’acceptation du québec [caq] ).
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Apply for a provincial or territorial attestation letter Needed in most cases Get a provincial or territorial attestation letter (PAL/TAL) from your school. In most cases, you need to accept your offer and pay your tuition fees, either in part or in full, to get your PAL/TAL. If you’re studying in Quebec, you need a Quebec Acceptance Certificate (Certificat d’acceptation du Québec [CAQ]).

requirements.label: Copy of a valid passport or travel document
requirements.description: IRCC marks proof of identity 'always required', and requires it from you and from each family member who comes with you. Upload a copy of the information page when you apply online. If you are approved you must send IRCC your original passport.
requirements.source_excerpt: show proof of identity always required to show proof of identity, you (and each family member who comes with you) must have a copy of a valid passport or travel document
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Show proof of identity Always required To show proof of identity, you (and each family member who comes with you) must have a copy of a valid passport or travel document

requirements.label: Two recent passport-size photos
requirements.description: The name and date of birth of the person must be written on the back of each photo. IRCC lists this under proof of identity, which it marks 'always required'.

requirements.source_excerpt_display: 2 recent passport size photos The name and date of birth of the person must be written on the back of each photo.

requirements.label: Proof of funds
requirements.description: IRCC marks this 'always required'. The money must support you and any family members coming with you. The documents page publishes no amount and links out to a separate proof-of-funds page.
requirements.source_excerpt: show proof of funds always required to support yourself and any family members coming with you, you must show proof of funds .
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Show proof of funds Always required To support yourself and any family members coming with you, you must show proof of funds.

requirements.label: Immigration medical exam (upfront exam with a panel physician)
requirements.description: Needed when you will study in Canada for more than 6 months and have lived for 6 or more months in a row, in the year before you come, in a country or territory on IRCC's medical-exam list (Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nigeria, the Philippines and others). Guide 5269 lets you either have an upfront exam with a panel physician and upload proof of it with your application, or wait for the visa office to send medical instructions after you apply, so this slot does not block preparing your forms. IRCC's personalised checklist names the slot 'Request for Medical Exam'.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you plan to work, visit or study in canada for more than six months: you will need a medical exam if you: have lived temporarily for six or more months in a row: in any of these countries or territories in the one year immediately before the date you want to enter canada. ... if you have an upfront medical exam, you must submit proof that you completed the medical exam with your application.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you plan to work, visit or study in Canada for more than six months: You will need a medical exam if you: have lived temporarily for six or more months in a row: in any of these countries or territories in the one year immediately before the date you want to enter Canada. ... If you have an upfront medical exam, you must submit proof that you completed the medical exam with your application.

requirements.label: Proof of care for a minor child (appointed custodian)
requirements.description: IRCC marks this 'check if needed'. It applies to children under 17 who are not coming to Canada with a parent or legal guardian. IRCC publishes what to submit on a separate page.
requirements.source_excerpt: proof of care (for minor children in canada) check if needed children under the age of 17 who are not coming to canada with a parent or legal guardian must have an appointed custodian.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Proof of care (for minor children in Canada) Check if needed Children under the age of 17 who are not coming to Canada with a parent or legal guardian must have an appointed custodian.

requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you are married, you must send a photocopy of your marriage licence or certificate with your application.

requirements.label: Application for a Study Permit Made Outside of Canada
requirements.description: IRCC states each person requiring a study permit to come to Canada must complete this form, and that you download and complete it whether you apply in the IRCC secure account or on paper. The form is titled for applications made outside Canada; applicants applying from inside Canada or at a port of entry follow a different route, which was not extracted.

requirements.source_excerpt_display: Application for Study Permit Made Outside of Canada (IMM 1294) Who must fill out this application form? Each person requiring a study permit to come to Canada must complete this form.

requirements.label: Family Information Form – Visitors, Students and Workers
requirements.description: Completed by each person 18 or older applying for a study permit outside Canada: you, your spouse or common-law partner, your parents, your children and your brothers and sisters, with whether each will come to Canada with you. IRCC's secure-account checklist names it 'Family Information'; guide 5269's paper list names the same form IMM 5707.
requirements.source_excerpt: this form must be completed by each person, 18 years of age or older, applying for a temporary resident visa, a study or work permit outside canada.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: This form must be completed by each person, 18 years of age or older, applying for a Temporary Resident Visa, a study or work permit outside Canada.

requirements.description: Required by the IMM 1294 instructions where the applicant is in a common-law union.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you are in a common-law union, you must also fill out the statutory declaration of common-law union [imm 5409] (opens in a new tab) form and include it with your application.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you are in a common-law union, you must also fill out the Statutory Declaration of Common-law Union [IMM 5409] (opens in a new tab) form and include it with your application.

requirements.label: Use of a Representative
requirements.source_excerpt: if you wish to have a representative who can conduct business on your behalf, you must give us their email and mailing addresses in this section and fill out the use of a representative imm 5476 (opens in a new tab) form.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you wish to have a representative who can conduct business on your behalf, you must give us their email and mailing addresses in this section and fill out the Use of a Representative IMM 5476 (opens in a new tab) form.
requirements.description: Required when anyone — paid or unpaid, including a friend or relative — represents you on this application. Complete and sign IMM 5476, have your representative sign it, and upload it with your application. A paid representative must be authorized (a licensed immigration consultant, a lawyer or a Quebec notary in good standing). Your representative can never sign the application for you.

requirements.label: Apply online
requirements.description: IRCC states study permit applications must be submitted online whether you are outside Canada or already in Canada. It names two exceptions: a disability that prevents applying online, or holding an identity or travel document for non-national residents, refugees or stateless persons.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you’re applying for a study permit, you must apply online , whether you’re outside of canada or already in canada. you’re only eligible to apply on paper if you have a disability that prevents you from applying online hold an identity or travel document for non-national residents, refugees or stateless persons
requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you’re applying for a study permit, you must apply online, whether you’re outside of Canada or already in Canada. You’re only eligible to apply on paper if you have a disability that prevents you from applying online hold an identity or travel document for non-national residents, refugees or stateless persons

requirements.label: Create an IRCC secure account
requirements.description: IRCC states an account is needed to pay fees, submit the application and check its status.
requirements.source_excerpt: you need an account to apply online. you can use your account to: pay your fees submit your application check the status of your application
requirements.source_excerpt_display: You need an account to apply online. You can use your account to: pay your fees submit your application check the status of your application

requirements.label: Give your biometrics (fingerprints and photograph)
requirements.description: IRCC states applicants between 14 and 79 probably need to give biometrics, and that they are only given once every 10 years. Once IRCC sends the letter telling you to give biometrics you have 30 days to do so. Whether you need to give them also depends on your citizenship; IRCC publishes a separate tool to check, and that country list has not been extracted.
requirements.source_excerpt: if you’re between 14 and 79 years old, you probably need to give your fingerprints and photo (biometrics).you only need to give your biometrics once every 10 years to make repeat trips to canada easier.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: If you’re between 14 and 79 years old, you probably need to give your fingerprints and photo (biometrics).You only need to give your biometrics once every 10 years to make repeat trips to Canada easier.

requirements.label: Immigration medical exam
requirements.description: IRCC marks this 'check if needed' and names three triggers: planning to stay in Canada for more than 6 months, recently spending time in certain countries, or planning to work in certain jobs where public health must be protected. Only the first is expressible from the facts VisaAI collects, and gating on it alone would hide the requirement from applicants caught by the other two, so no rule is attached.
requirements.source_excerpt: get a medical exam check if needed you may need a medical exam if any of these situations apply to you: you plan to stay in canada for more than 6 months. you recently spent time in certain countries. you plan to work in certain jobs where public health must be protected.
requirements.source_excerpt_display: Get a medical exam Check if needed You may need a medical exam if any of these situations apply to you: You plan to stay in Canada for more than 6 months. You recently spent time in certain countries. You plan to work in certain jobs where public health must be protected.

requirements.label: Police certificate
requirements.description: IRCC marks this 'check if needed' and states only that it may ask for one in some cases. It advises applying as early as possible if you think you might need one.

requirements.source_excerpt_display: Get a police certificate Check if needed In some cases, we may ask you for a police certificate. If you think you might need one, you should apply for one as early as possible.

requirements.description: IRCC marks this 'recommended' rather than required, though the sentence itself reads 'you must explain'. It should explain why you want to study in Canada and that you understand your responsibilities as an international student.
